parts.title: The Top of the World
parts.text: The research plane touched down on the ice of the **polar** north, and Freya felt her breath freeze before it left her scarf. The view was **stark**: no trees, no buildings, only an endless white plain meeting a pale sky. Tariq, the team's **navigator**, studied his compass and shook his head. "This place is **inhospitable**," he warned. "The land does not care whether we survive, so we must never take chances."

parts.title: Camp Life
parts.text: Dominic, the team's medic, drilled into the **permafrost**, ground that stays frozen all year long, to collect samples. He made everyone wear layers of wool and down to **insulate** their bodies, because bare skin could suffer **frostbite** in minutes. That night, ribbons of green light, the **aurora**, rippled across the black sky, and for a while nobody noticed the cold.

parts.title: A Dangerous Morning
parts.text: The next day the team crossed a **floe**, a flat sheet of sea ice, to reach the huge **iceberg** they had traveled so far to measure. Halfway across, Tariq froze and raised his fist. A hidden **crevasse**, a deep crack covered by thin snow, lay inches from Freya's boot. Before anyone could speak, a **whiteout** swallowed the world, with snow so thick that she could not see her own hands. They tied themselves to one rope and crept along, one slow step at a time.

parts.title: Back to Camp
parts.text: Hours later, the wind finally dropped and the camp lights appeared ahead. Freya understood the Arctic's only rule: plan carefully, listen to your teammates, and never stop paying attention. She fell asleep that night grateful for every one of them.

definitions.meaning1: A huge mass of ice that has broken off a glacier and floats in the sea. Example: Most of the iceberg hides below the surface of the water.
definitions.studentChallenge: The captain steered carefully to avoid the drifting ___ that loomed in the fog.

definitions.meaning1: Ground that stays frozen all year, sometimes for thousands of years. Example: Builders had to dig through permafrost to lay the pipeline.
definitions.studentChallenge: As the climate warms, melting ___ is releasing gases that were trapped underground.

definitions.meaning1: To cover or protect something so that heat, cold or sound cannot easily pass through. Example: Thick foam helps insulate the walls so the house stays warm all winter.
definitions.meaning2: To protect someone from unpleasant experiences. Example: Parents cannot always insulate their children from disappointment.
definitions.studentChallenge: Thick wool socks ___ your feet from the freezing ground.

definitions.meaning1: Damage to the skin and body tissue caused by extreme cold. Example: Without gloves, she risked frostbite in her fingers after only a few minutes outside.
definitions.studentChallenge: The hiker lost two toes to ___ after being stranded on the mountain.

definitions.meaning1: Colorful lights that glow and ripple in the sky near the North and South Poles. Example: Travelers book trips to Iceland each winter hoping to see the aurora dance overhead.
definitions.studentChallenge: Green and violet light rippled across the night sky in a glowing ___.

definitions.meaning1: Of or near the North Pole or the South Pole. Example: Penguins and seals thrive in the polar regions at the bottom of the world.
definitions.meaning2: Completely opposite, as in polar opposites. Example: The twins have polar opposite tastes in music.
definitions.studentChallenge: Scientists wore heavy parkas to study the ___ ice cap.

definitions.meaning1: A person who plans and directs the route of a ship, plane or vehicle. Example: The ship's navigator studied the stars and charts to plot a safe course.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ called out each turn while the driver steered through the storm.

definitions.meaning1: A deep, narrow crack in a glacier or ice sheet. Example: Rescuers lowered a rope into the narrow crevasse where the explorer had fallen.
definitions.studentChallenge: A hidden ___ lay under the snow, so the climbers tested every step.

definitions.meaning1: A large, flat sheet of ice floating on the sea. Example: The seal rested on a flat floe drifting slowly past the ship.
definitions.studentChallenge: Researchers pitched their tents on a thick ___ that floated in the bay.

definitions.meaning1: A snowstorm or thick fog in which everything looks white and nothing else can be seen. Example: In the whiteout, the hikers could not see their own boots.
definitions.studentChallenge: A sudden ___ swallowed the road, so the driver pulled over until it passed.

definitions.meaning1: Plain, bare and harsh. Example: The desert was a stark landscape with no trees, water or shade.
definitions.meaning2: Sharp and impossible to miss. Example: There was a stark difference between how the two teams played.
definitions.studentChallenge: The ___ white plain stretched to the horizon with nothing on it.

definitions.meaning1: Not welcoming; hard to live in or visit because conditions are harsh. Example: Few animals can survive in the inhospitable desert, where the sun is brutal.
definitions.meaning2: Unfriendly toward visitors. Example: The innkeeper's cold, inhospitable manner made guests want to leave.
definitions.studentChallenge: The mountain's thin air and freezing wind made it ___ to travelers.
